$comment: Packages whose path in coverage-baseline.json changed, old path to new path.
`pnpm coverage:ratchet` compares the baseline with the merge base by key, so a renamed
package looks exactly like a deleted floor plus a new one, and the gate refuses it. An
entry here tells the ratchet that the floor moved rather than vanished.
It is not a way to lower a floor. The ratchet reads an entry only once the old key has left
the baseline, and then compares the new key against the old floor metric by metric: a
lower number, a missing metric or a `not_configured` replacement is a finding exactly as
it would be for a package that was never renamed (`scripts/lib/coverage-floor-ratchet.test.mjs`).
This file names the old path, which the retired-name gate otherwise forbids, so it is the
one exempt file for that reason (`RETIRED_NAME_EXEMPTIONS`). An entry is dead weight once the
merge base has the new key, and can be deleted then; leaving it does no harm.
